children: The Contract Works comprise the complete design, supply, off-loading, distribution, setting-out and installation of the Contract Works, all as detailed within this Scope of Works and in accordance with the Contract.{br}
The Contract includes, but is not limited to:{br}
{b:Working Hours:} The Works are to be executed between {Mon-Fri} Monday to Friday and {Sat} Saturday and the Contractor is to allow for all costs associated with working during these hours.{br}

The Contractor is deemed to have visited the site, to have taken into account all local and existing conditions and to be thoroughly acquainted with the position and accessibility of the Contract works and the conditions under which they will have to be carried out. Claims based on lack of knowledge will not be entertained.{br}

{CompanyName} shall not provide any site security personnel. The Contractor is therefore to make arrangements and be responsible for all its material and plant. All materials and plant left on site is at the Contractors own risk.{br}

When undertaking the design of the Contract Works, the Contractor shall use all the reasonable skill, care and diligence to be expected of an architect, or other professionally qualified designer, who is experienced in undertaking design of an equal or similar nature, size and complexity to that of the Contract Works.{br}

The Contractor is to ensure its design is in accordance with the Contract documents, employers requirements, British Standards, and Industry regulations, including but not limited to the Building Regulations.{br}

No provision of this Contract shall operate to exclude or restrict the Contractors liability under statute or common law for any goods and materials he shall supply, or has supplied, for use on, or incorporation in the Contract Works.{br}
The Contractor is to follow the Design Submission Procedure as provided for in Schedule 6 of the JCT Conditions.{br}

children.name: text
children: The Contractoris to ensure its design is in accordance with the Contract documents, employers requirements, British Standards, and Industry regulations, including but not limited to the Building Regulations.{br}
The Contractor shall be responsible for the management of the Contract programme and will produce and regularly update a programme - providing a copy of such to {CompanyName} as upon request.{br}
The Contractor must adhere to all aspects of {CompanyName} Project Quality Procedures, Health & Safety Plan and Management Protocols.{br}

The Contractor shall submit a formal Method Statement plus Risk Assessments for all site activities to {CompanyName} for review, comment and approval ahead of commencement on site, not less than 7 days prior to its proposed start date on site.{br}
The Contract Works shall not be further subcontracted without the express permission of {CompanyName}.{br}

All operatives engaged in the execution of the Contract Works must be experienced and skilled in their particular discipline and appropriately qualified. Additionally, all operatives shall be CSCS certified.{br}

All personnel operating mechanical plant must be fully and properly trained and possess a valid certificate of training and competence. All personnel constructing scaffolding or mobile towers must be properly trained and in possession of valid certification. Copies of all operatives qualifications/certifications, together with National Insurance details must be provided to {CompanyName} if requested.{br}

{CompanyName} may provide a primary datum and gridlines for the site. If this is the case, the Contractor is then responsible for detailed setting out/site measurement/survey of the Contract Works from and therefore the correct positioning of each element.{br}

The Contractor will be responsible for logistical planning, taking delivery of, unloading and distributing all component elements of the Contract Works. If distribution assistance is required this may be possible subject to prior agreement with {CompanyName}. In all cases however, the slinger/banksman is the responsibility of the Contractor and {CompanyName} do not accept any liability for handling the Contractors goods and materials.{br}

The Contractor shall be responsible for all plant items provided by {CompanyName} when they are under the control of the Contractor. Any damage rectification costs to the said items will be the responsibility of the Contractor. All other plant items and equipment necessary for the complete installation of the Contract Works will be provided by the Contractor.{br}
The Contractor must allow for all reasonable measures required to overcome the effects of adverse weather.{br}

The Contractor will be responsible for all Contract materials and tools on site. The Contractor will supply all small tools (associated accessories & consumables) plus any temporary task lighting, necessary for the execution of the Contract works in their entirety.{br}
The Contractor shall provide all other installation accessories, including but not restricted to Heras (or equivalent) fencing, all requisite signage, and installation plant.{br}

The Contractor shall wipe down all elements of the Contract Works to ensure that all labels, plus any marks associated with installation and storage, are The Employer’s Agent as part of the installation process.{br}

The Contractor shall supply, install, reasonably maintain, The Employer’s Agent and dispose of protection materials for the Contract Works. The risk in the Contract Works shall remain with the Contract until Practical Completion.{br}

The Contractor must take all reasonable measures to ensure that no damage is caused to works of any other trade. Any damage will be notified to the Contractor with the associated costs deducted from monies due to the Contractor or recovered as a debt. The Contractor has included for all necessary provisions to ensure that the Client is able to achieve the appropriate certification/approval from Building Control.{br}
The Contractor must adhere and allow for complying with all {CompanyName} and Statutory Health and Safety requirements.{br}
All electrical tools and appliances must be inspected, tagged and maintained in accordance with prevalent safety legislation.{br}

The Contractor is to provide his operatives with all necessary protective equipment free of charge, including but not restricted to hard hats, safety boots, high visibility vests, goggles, gloves and safety harnesses.{br}
The Contractor shall ensure that a high standard of housekeeping is maintained throughout the Contract  Works, with all arisings broken down, de-nailed (if necessary) and deposited in skips.{br}

The Contractor shall The Employer’s Agent all plant, equipment and facilities associated with the Contract Works from site as and when directed by {CompanyName} or upon the completion of the Contract works, whichever is the sooner.{br}
The Contractor is required to hold and maintain the following insurances throughout the Contract works:{br}

children: Where the Contractor has been instructed in writing by the Client  to carry out any additional or substitute work on a daywork basis the Contractor shall be paid for such work in accordance with the provisions of the Contractor and at the rates and prices set out in this daywork schedule; provided always that payment on a daywork basis is conditional upon:{br}
The Contractor having given the Client reasonable notice of the commencement of any work for which the Contractor intends to seek payment on a daywork basis.{br}

The Contractor maintaining contemporary records (daywork sheets) of all resources engaged upon the instructed daywork (including the names and site pass/NI No's of all operatives) and delivering such records to the Client's Project Manager or Quantity Surveyor each day during the currency of the instructed daywork for endorsement or comment.{br}

NB. For the avoidance of endorsement of any daywork sheet by the Client will constitute verification of resource expenditure only. Daywork hours must be recorded net (exclusive of all meal/refreshments breaks and travel time).{br}

Endorsed daywork sheets together with any further substantive information shall be included within the Contractor's interim application for payment, with the daywork sheets fully priced, extended and totalled prior to submission. Further, all daywork sheets shall be specifically referenced to the Client's instruction.{br}

All labour rates herein are fully inclusive of all direct and indirect costs including but not restricted to the Contractor's overheads and profit, head office charges, site management, supervision and other preliminary costs, PPE, small tools and consumables, all direct and indirect employee costs and all other charges, and shall not be subject to any further adjustment. All rates included herein are fixed and firm for the duration of the Works.{br}

The Contractor labour rates shall include for the amount of wages to be paid to the work people inclusive of all overheads and profits and such extra payments of differentials as are paid in respect of staff responsibility, discomfort, inconvenience and risk in accordance with the rules and awards of the recognised wage fixing bodies of the trades concerned.{br}

The Contractor labour rates shall include for the amount of wages to be paid to the work people inclusive of all overheads and profits and such extra payments of differentials as are paid in respect of staff responsibility, discomfort, inconvenience and risk in accordance with the rules and awards of the recognised wage fixing bodies of the trades concerned.{br}

Where the Contractor is instructed to supply materials to execute daywork the Contractor shall be reimbursed the actual and reasonable net cost of the material, plus the additional percentage stated herein. For the avoidance of doubt the noted additional percentage shall cater for all direct and indirect costs associated with the supply of the materials, including but not restricted to the Contractor's overheads and profit, all delivery, off-loading and further handling costs, the disposal of packaging and arisings associated with the materials from site and any further statutory or other costs.{br}
The Contractor must insert below, various categories of craftsmen, labourers, apprentices, etc., he proposes to use, and the hourly rates, calculated as before described.{br}
